{:db/id 17592186124470 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186124277 :question/id #uuid "033e459e-5148-5e78-ab5c-7e455b06cd64" :question/math-academy-id "e-3695" :question/problem "If $f(x,y,z) = xz\ln{y}$ and $\mathbf r (t) =  t^2 \, \mathbf i + t  \, \mathbf j +t^3  \, \mathbf k,$ compute $\dfrac {\textrm d}{\textrm d t} [f(\mathbf r(t))].$" :question/worked-solution "The chain rule in vector form states that

\dfrac {\textrm d}{\textrm d t} [f(\mathbf r (t))] = \nabla f(\mathbf r(t)) \cdot \mathbf r'(t).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{∇}f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz\operatorname{ln}y)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xz\operatorname{ln}y)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz\operatorname{ln}y)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =z\operatorname{ln}y\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{xz}{y}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+x\operatorname{ln}y\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x= t^2,$ $y = t$ and $z= t^3$ into the above to find $\nabla f(\mathbf{r}(t)){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{∇}f(\mathbf{r}(t)) & ={t}^{3}\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{t}^{4}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =2t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+3{t}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
